messages:
Maya L: hey team :wave: day 2 here. i'm blocked cloning from git.internal.redwood.com when running inside a container. host clones fine when connected to corp-vpn (OpenConnect + Okta). DNS inside the container returns NXDOMAIN.
Jorge P: welcome! quick checks: can you ping the hostname from your host and from inside the container? also paste /etc/resolv.conf from both the host and the container.
Maya L: host:
```
$ ping git.internal.redwood.com
PING git.internal.redwood.com (10.12.4.10): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 10.12.4.10: icmp_seq=0 ttl=64 time=12.3 ms
```
host /etc/resolv.conf:
```
# Generated by NetworkManager
nameserver 127.0.0.53
search redwood.internal
```
container /etc/resolv.conf:
```
nameserver 8.8.8.8
```
container: `ping git.internal.redwood.com` -> ping: unknown host git.internal.redwood.com
Nina R: looks like systemd-resolved's stub resolver (127.0.0.53) is on the host and docker/container only get the external DNS (8.8.8.8). containers don't see the host's stub by default. options: 1) configure docker daemon to use the VPN/internal DNS, 2) run container with `--network=host` (linux only), 3) pass `--dns` or `--add-host` to the container, or 4) use an SSH/SOCKS proxy through the bastion.
Jorge P: to add the VPN DNS to docker permanently, on the host create /etc/docker/daemon.json (or edit) with:
```
{
  "dns": ["10.12.0.2", "8.8.8.8"]
}
```
then `sudo systemctl restart docker`. Replace 10.12.0.2 with your VPN nameserver.
Nina R: one-off test without restarting docker: `docker run --rm --dns 10.12.0.2 busybox nslookup git.internal.redwood.com` — should resolve. Or add an entry to `/etc/hosts` for quick work: `--add-host=git.internal.redwood.com:10.12.4.10`.
Maya L: tried `docker run --rm --dns 10.12.0.2 busybox nslookup git.internal.redwood.com` and it NOW resolves, thanks! question: why can't the container reach 127.0.0.53?
IT Ops: because 127.0.0.53 is a loopback on the host's network namespace, not reachable from container network namespace. exposing systemd-resolved to containers can be done but is fragile. another approach on linux: `sudo ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf` so the actual nameserver IPs are in /etc/resolv.conf (be careful, this changes host resolver behavior).
Jorge P: alternative if you prefer SSH-based git: you can proxy via the bastion: `ssh -J alex@bastion.redwood.com git@10.12.4.10` or set `GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o ProxyCommand="ssh -W %h:%p alex@bastion.redwood.com"' git clone git@internal:repo.git`. For HTTP(S) git, using host port-forward is also an option: `ssh -L 9418:10.12.4.10:9418 alex@bastion.redwood.com` then `git clone git://localhost:9418/repo.git`.
Nina R: note for mac users with Colima/Lima: DNS is handled by the VM; see eng-infra docs. We'll add a brief troubleshooting section explaining `--dns`, daemon.json, and `--add-host`.
infra-bot: ticket INF-4890 created to add "DNS + containers with VPN" troubleshooting to onboarding docs (assigned eng-infra).
Maya L: cloning works now, thanks everyone :tada: appreciate the quick help!
